caption: Arcosh(-Infinity) is +Infinity, not -Infinity -- the principal branch keeps $\Re(\operatorname{arcosh} z) \ge 0$ everywhere

wolfram.note: Branch-cut form differs: 1/sqrt(x^2-1) (ours, CE-native) vs 1/(sqrt(x-1)sqrt(x+1)) (Wolfram); equal on the principal real domain x>1, differ off it. Not one of our patches.

Same branch-cut convention difference as D[ArcCosh[x],x]: x*arccosh(x) - sqrt(x^2-1) (ours) vs x*arccosh(x) - sqrt(x-1)*sqrt(x+1) (Wolfram) -- equal antiderivatives on the principal real domain, differ off it.

Real bug, but the fix lives in packages/ce-patches/src/compute-engine/library/trigonometry.ts's evaluateHyperbolicInverseAtInfinity (locked to lane A-125, not edited here). That function deliberately sets Arcosh(ComplexInfinity) = ComplexInfinity, citing DLMF 4.37.16/4.37.19 ('Arsinh and Arcosh grow like ln|2z| in every direction ... so they are ComplexInfinity there'). Verified live against real Wolfram: ArcSinh[ComplexInfinity] IS ComplexInfinity (matches the patch), but ArcCosh[ComplexInfinity] and Log[ComplexInfinity] both give Infinity (real, directed), not ComplexInfinity -- the magnitude of log(z) diverges along the positive real axis regardless of z's own phase, since Re(log z) -> +Infinity while Im(log z) stays bounded, so its own direction -> 0. The patch's Arcosh case looks like a genuine oversight distinguishing it from Arsinh's (correct) case -- flagging precisely for A-125 to fix in their file.
